notes: WHY THE SUBJECT READ 78, term by term. drep 0.000, no tracking (2011), DBPM +1.3 = the 0.848 percentile of its season, 6'6", 2,426 minutes. His perdef composite PD is 0.511 and his no-vote cap min(PD, 0.62) is 0.511 — card 51. recal_55's pre-2014 relief then fired: max(cap, min(0.80, 0.28 + 0.60 * 0.848)) = 0.7887 = card 78.29, smoothed to 78. One hundred percent of the ruling's complaint was that one line, and that line reads exactly ONE input, the within-season DBPM percentile.

THE PLATEAU WAS THE FAULT. 0.28 + 0.60 * P reached its 0.80 ceiling at P = 0.867, so every no-vote pre-2014 card in the top 13% of its season's DBPM was handed the identical maximum: Ron Harper '88 (P 0.919), Brent Barry '02 (0.920), Craig Ehlo '89 (0.932) and Carlos Delfino '11 (0.926) all read the same 78 the subject did, at the same height, on visibly different defensive careers. 0.28 + 0.52 * P reaches 0.80 only at P = 1.0, so the ceiling is a single point instead of the top eighth of every season and the class is ranked again: 75 / 73 / 74 / 74 against the subject's 73.

THE 0.80 CEILING STAYS, and is now exactly the value at P = 1.0 rather than a plateau — the min() is retained as the explicit statement of the channel's top, so a later ruling that wants a different top has one number to change.

MILDEST WAS MEASURED AND REJECTED ON THE RULING'S OWN WORDS. recal_134's variant B (slope 0.54) is the mildest re-cut that reaches the band: the subject lands on 74, which is the CEILING of 72 +-2 and is not 'low 70s'. It also leaves a residual plateau over the top 3.7% of each season (0.80 reached at P = 0.963), i.e. it shrinks the artefact instead of retiring it. 0.52 lands 73, retires the plateau completely, and costs the SAME anchor set — the three that fail under 0.54 are the three that fail under 0.52, two of them released by his ruling. Footprint of the difference: 5,184 perdef cards move at 0.52 against 5,014 at 0.54; max |move| 8 against 6.
NOBODY ROSE. Zero risers on perdef, def and ovr; the single OFF move in the whole pool is Danny Granger '06 o_ovr 44 -> 45, a rounding artefact of the OVR blend, not a channel.

2014+ IS UNTOUCHED, by construction and by measurement. The relief is gated `if yr < 2014 and r['drep'] <= 0.05` and writes only `novote`, which feeds only that card's PD2 — it never touches PD, so the within-season Pvot pool every voted card is ranked in is bit-identical. Of 3,016 cards with peak_season >= 2014, exactly 83 moved on perdef and ALL 83 are peak_season 2014, reached only because the 20/60/20 season blend gives a 2014 card 20% of its 2013 neighbour. peak_season 2015 and later: ZERO, on perdef, DEF and OVR.

THE TWO RELEASED PINS, and why the ruling could not land without them. recal_134 declined this exact ruling and named them. Caron Butler '08 sits BELOW the subject on the only input this channel reads (DBPM percentile 0.826 vs 0.848) and below him on every other perdef input, so no monotone re-cut lowers Ginóbili without lowering Butler at least as much; he was standing on the floor of his own 73 +-1 band with 0.0123 of DEF headroom. Vlade Divac '95 is recal_55's OWN relief anchor, and holding him at 77+ while taking the subject to 73 needs a nine-point cliff across 0.032 of DBPM percentile — the plateau-with-a-cliff shape recal_20 and recal_82 exist to remove. Tomer released both: 'Agree with Manu'.

THE ONE EXPECTED ANCHOR MISS IS NOT AN ATTRIBUTE MISS. Bulls '96 team:defdial (r94, 99 tol 0) reads 93 on this branch because Ron Harper '96, Toni Kukoč '96, Luc Longley '96 and Steve Kerr '96 are all no-vote cards in this class. The dial is a FROZEN scale in src/engine/gauges.ts, which this agent does not own and did not touch; the integrator re-derives the DEF block with scripts/gauge100.ts, whose DEF_TOP is defined as the Bulls '96 five's own adjusted drtgRef, so they return to 99 at integration by construction. Their raw drtgRef moved 107.5589 -> 107.8814, and their ALL-TIME rank among the 1,255 wheel best-fives moved 5 -> 8 — they were already not rank 1 on main, so the summit convention is unaffected.

THE OTHER TWO DIALS, for the record: Jazz '98 DEF 91 -> 85 (drtgRef 108.0394 -> 108.3520), Spurs '11 DEF 58 -> 51 (109.6220 -> 109.9446). Both are unpinned and both fall for the same reason as the Bulls — their no-vote defenders were sitting on the plateau. Every pinned dial except the Bulls holds: Pistons '04 84 +-4, Lakers '87 67 +-6 (reads 61), Warriors '17 81 +-5 (reads 76), 76ers '85 93 +-2, Celtics '24 65 +-3, Thunder '26, Pistons '26, 76ers '26.
